mainTopic: Other ways to understand ריש לקיש's teaching, and how he learns both touching and eating קודש while טמא from 'בכל קדש לא תגע'
overview: On the previous עמוד, עולא said in the name of ריש לקיש that a טמא who puts his hand into the עזרה gets מלקות. A question was raised from the case of the מצורע. Here רבינא answers that ריש לקיש meant only מלקות, not כרת. Then רבין reports in the name of רבי אבהו that ריש לקיש's teaching was really about a טמא who touches קודש. ריש לקיש says such a person gets מלקות, from the פסוק 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. רבי יוחנן says he does not, because that פסוק is about תרומה. The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: he already uses this פסוק as the אזהרה against a טמא eating קודש. רבי יוחנן learns that אזהרה from a גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו' instead. The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש learns touching from the word 'תגע' and eating from the היקש of קודש to מקדש. A ברייתא then supports ריש לקיש, and its explanation of that היקש continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבינא: the teaching was only about lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers the question from the מצורע differently than עולא did. ריש לקיש's teaching was only about מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It was said only regarding lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a new answer to the question raised against ריש לקיש's rule that partial entry into the עזרה counts as entry. He says ריש לקיש only meant that the person gets מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question came from the מצורע, where partial entry does not count. רבינא answers that ריש לקיש never said partial entry is fully like full entry. It counts for the לאו and its מלקות, but not for כרת. So the two cases do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes, the punishment for breaking a לאו
Regarding, with respect to

phrases.english: Ravina said:
phrases.notes: He's answering the question from the end of the previous עמוד, about the מצורע who goes in only partway.

phrases.english: It was said regarding lashes.
phrases.notes: In other words, partial entry gets מלקות, but not כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, after עולא's answer on the previous עמוד, to the question from the מצורע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule to one kind of punishment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's teaching seemed to treat partial entry as full entry in every way, which clashes with the מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partial entry counts only for the לאו and its מלקות, not for כרת.

steps.title: רבין's version: the teaching was about touching sacred food
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a report from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי אבהו. ריש לקיש's teaching was really about a טמא who touches קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי אבהו said: It was said regarding an impure person who touched sacred food.
steps.whatsHappening: A whole different version of ריש לקיש's teaching arrives with רבין. In this version ריש לקיש's teaching is about a טמא touching קודש, not about entering the עזרה. The next step will quote that teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא and רבינא both understood the teaching to be about a טמא entering the עזרה. In רבין's version it has nothing to do with entering at all. Because of that, the question from the מצורע and partial entry never even comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A person who is ritually impure
Touched
Sacred food, such as meat of קרבנות

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
Rabbi Abbahu said:
It was said regarding an impure person who touched sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the whole setting of ריש לקיש's teaching instead of just narrowing it, as רבינא did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש's teaching about מלקות was about a טמא touching קודש, not about entering the עזרה.

steps.title: The dispute: is an impure person who touches sacred food flogged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the מחלוקת. ריש לקיש says a טמא who touches קודש gets מלקות, and רבי יוחנן says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was said: An impure person who touched sacred food — ריש לקיש said he is flogged; רבי יוחנן said he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the מחלוקת that רבין was talking about. It gives the bottom line of each side first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about whether a טמא who touches קודש gets מלקות. That depends on whether the תורה has a לאו against touching קודש. The next step gives each side's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: He gets lashes
He does not get lashes

phrases.english: As it was said:
An impure person who touched sacred food —
Reish Lakish said: He is flogged,
Rabbi Yochanan said: He is not flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the full teaching that רבין referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: a טמא who touches קודש gets מלקות. רבי יוחנן: he does not.

steps.title: Each side's reason: what does the verse about touching refer to?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns his rule from 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. רבי יוחנן says that פסוק is about תרומה, not קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said he is flogged, because it says 'Every sacred thing she shall not touch.' רבי יוחנן said he is not flogged, because that verse is written about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each side holds what he does. Both are arguing about the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, 'קדש' in the פסוק means real קודש, so there is a לאו against touching it, and a לאו brings מלקות. רבי יוחנן reads 'קדש' there as תרומה. That leaves no לאו for touching קודש, so there are no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Every sacred thing she shall not touch' (ויקרא 12:4)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
It is written

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides are reading the very same פסוק. They are not arguing about whether there is a source at all. They are arguing about whether 'קדש' in that פסוק means real קודש or תרומה.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said he is flogged —
"Every sacred thing she shall not touch."
And Rabbi Yochanan said he is not flogged —
That verse is written about terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר לוֹקֶה – בְּכׇל קֹדֶשׁ לֹא תִגָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the two positions in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a טמא who touches קודש gets מלקות
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 12:4, 'בכל קדש לא תגע', read as קודש by ריש לקיש and as תרומה by רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Challenge: ריש לקיש already uses this verse for eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש can use 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for touching. He needs that פסוק as the אזהרה against a טמא eating בשר קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש — does this verse really come for this? He needs it for the warning against eating sacred meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's source. That same פסוק is already busy teaching a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is usually taken to teach one main law. If ריש לקיש uses this פסוק as the אזהרה for a טמא who eats קודש, it seems to be used up. Then it cannot also give a separate לאו with מלקות for touching.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this פסוק really come to teach this?
He needs it (for something else)
A warning; the לאו that forbids an act
Meat of קרבנות

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish —
Does this verse come for this?!
He needs this for:
The warning against one who eats sacred meat!
phrases.notes: Meaning a טמא who eats meat of קרבנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ – הַאי קְרָא לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source ריש לקיש gave in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's use of 'בכל קדש לא תגע' as a לאו against touching קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש himself uses this פסוק for the אזהרה against a טמא eating קודש, so it seems unavailable for a separate law about touching.

steps.title: Proof that ריש לקיש uses this verse for eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting ריש לקיש's own teaching. 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is his source for the אזהרה against a טמא eating בשר קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was said: From where do we know the warning against eating sacred meat? ריש לקיש said: 'Every sacred thing she shall not touch.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the challenge from step 5 by showing ריש לקיש's own words. He does use this פסוק for eating, so the question stands for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here ריש לקיש himself reads 'לא תגע' (do not touch) as being about eating. That makes the question sharper: how can the same פסוק give two separate לאוין, one for eating and one for touching? Step 8 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
For one who eats

phrases.english: As it was said:
From where do we know the warning against one who eats sacred meat?
phrases.notes: Again, this means a טמא who eats it.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
"Every sacred thing she shall not touch."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: אַזְהָרָה לָאוֹכֵל בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶשׁ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 5 by quoting ריש לקיש's own teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That ריש לקיש needs 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for the law about eating
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's teaching that the אזהרה against a טמא eating בשר קודש comes from 'בכל קדש לא תגע'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's different source for the warning against eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting ברדלא, learns the אזהרה against a טמא eating קודש from a גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו'–'טומאתו', comparing it to entering the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: ברדלא taught that we learn it from the word 'his impurity' here and 'his impurity' by entering the מקדש. Just as there the תורה gave a punishment and also a warning, so too here it gave a punishment and also a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the earlier מחלוקת. Here רבי יוחנן gives his own source for the warning against a טמא eating קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a טמא who eats קודש and a טמא who enters the מקדש are called 'טומאתו' in the פסוקים. Entering the מקדש has both a punishment and an explicit warning, so the גזירה שוה gives eating קודש a warning too. This shows that the main point of the quote stands: ריש לקיש uses 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for eating, while רבי יוחנן uses this גזירה שוה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned from (a גזירה שוה)
His impurity; the shared word that links the two cases
Entering the בית המקדש
The תורה gave a punishment and also a warning (אזהרה)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is still part of the quote that began in the previous step. It is not a new answer. It shows that ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן each have a different source for the warning against eating.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Bardela teaches:
It is learned from "his impurity" and "his impurity" written about entering the Temple;
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are ויקרא 7:20 (eating קודש) and במדבר 19:13 (entering the מקדש).

phrases.english: just as there, it gave a punishment and a warning,
so too here, it gave a punishment and a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted מחלוקת begun in step 6, giving רבי יוחנן's side
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, the אזהרה for a טמא eating קודש comes from a גזירה שוה with entering the מקדש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns both touching and eating from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns touching from the word 'תגע', and eating from the היקש of קודש to מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טמא who touched קודש: we learn it because the תורה used a word of touching. The warning for one who eats: we learn it because קודש is put side by side with מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5. ריש לקיש can learn two separate things from one פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that ריש לקיש needs 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for eating, so how can he also use it for touching? The answer is that the plain word 'תגע' (touch) teaches touching. The fact that the פסוק places קודש next to 'ואל המקדש לא תבא' teaches eating, through a היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה expressed it (literally, the Merciful One brought it out)
A word that means touching
It is compared through a היקש (placed side by side in the פסוק)
Learning a law by putting two things next to each other in a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one פסוק can carry two laws: one from its plain words and one from how it is placed next to something else.

phrases.english: An impure person who touched sacred food:
from the fact that the Torah expressed it with a word of touching;
the warning for one who eats:
from the fact that sacred food is compared to the Temple.
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 12:4, 'don't touch קודש' sits right next to 'don't come into the מקדש'.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָמֵא שֶׁנָּגַע בַּקּוֹדֶשׁ מִדְּאַפְּקַהּ רַחֲמָנָא בִּלְשׁוֹן נְגִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of steps 5 and 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one פסוק into two derivations: its words, and a היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ריש לקיש uses the פסוק for eating, it seemed he could not also use it for touching
steps.terutzMaskana: Touching comes from the word 'תגע', and eating comes from the היקש of קודש to מקדש

steps.title: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש and raises a question
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש: 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is a warning for one who eats. It then asks whether it might be only for one who touches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like ריש לקיש: 'Any holy thing she shall not touch' is a warning for one who eats. Do you say it is a warning for one who eats, or is it only for one who touches?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with ריש לקיש. The ברייתא first asks a question, which sets up its proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said this פסוק is about תרומה, but the ברייתא reads it as being about a טמא eating קודש, like ריש לקיש. The question 'maybe it is only about touching' is natural, because the פסוק literally says 'touch'.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
Do you say; the ברייתא testing its own reading
Or is it only; opening another possible reading
One who touches

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Reish Lakish:
"Any holy thing she shall not touch": this is a warning for one who eats.
Do you say it is a warning for one who eats;
or is it only for one who touches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending ריש לקיש, the גמרא brings outside support for him
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's reading of 'בכל קדש לא תגע' as an אזהרה for a טמא who eats קודש

steps.title: The ברייתא answers by comparing קודש to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves its reading from the היקש: the פסוק places קודש next to מקדש, so we compare them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Any holy thing she shall not touch, and into the מקדש she shall not come.' It compares קודש to מקדש. Just as the מקדש is something that carries...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The פסוק compares קודש to מקדש, the same היקש ריש לקיש used in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק puts קודש right next to מקדש, the two are compared. The ברייתא is starting to explain what they share: the מקדש is 'something that has...' something serious, and that leads to the case of eating. The sentence continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introducing the proof
It compares (makes a היקש)
A matter that has in it (the sentence continues)

steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of a sentence. The point of what the מקדש 'has' comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Any holy thing she shall not touch,
and into the Temple she shall not come":
it compares sacred food to the Temple;
just as the Temple is a matter that has in it

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: בְּכׇל קֹדֶשׁ לֹא תִגָּע וְאֶל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא תָבֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question the ברייתא raised in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is 'בכל קדש לא תגע' about eating or only about touching?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The היקש of קודש to מקדש shows it is about eating (the explanation continues past this point)
